items.title: Herbie Hancock interviewed by Michael Woods, New York City, New York, November 18, 1995
items.q: I was playing Bach inventions, some fugues and preludes and some Chopin. I had gotten into etudes and I think maybe Chopin’s “Fantasie Impromptu,” some things like that.

ctx.x: Now tell us about your debut with the symphony.

Well that was during the time that I was with Mrs. Jordan, the second teacher. By that time I was playing Bach inventions, some fugues and preludes and some Chopin. I had gotten into etudes and I think maybe Chopin’s “Fantasie Impromptu,” some things like that. So in 1950 — actually 1950, is that right? No — 1951 I auditioned for this — basically it was a concert. The Young People’s Concert Series in Chicago. And what would happen is that you would audition for who was then the Assistant Conductor of the Chicago…
